recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-26678 unless Patient Care later changes the intended meaning of Condition.onsetPeriod.
issue_request: FHIR-26678 was a Published FHIR-core Condition change request resolved as Persuasive with Modification. It asked Patient Care to clarify whether Condition.onsetPeriod meant progressive onset or an interval for imprecise onset; the approved comment says Period generally conveys an imprecise onset within the period and is not the transition period before diagnosis.
initial_application: The issue was applied by git commit 50ad212e27b70e1fb7ff98b988f6c5bc638cd051, which updated source/condition/condition-spreadsheet.xml with the approved Period comment. The old spreadsheet file is no longer present, but git history shows the phrase was carried through the later StructureDefinition source rework into source/condition/structuredefinition-Condition.xml.
additional_context: Condition is active in source/fhir.ini. The linked Zulip thread records the original ambiguity and Lloyd McKenzie's answer that onsetPeriod always means the onset occurred sometime within the period. The 2020-04-09 Patient Care minutes page references FHIR-26678. Later same-element decisions FHIR-32477 and FHIR-42978 added Range and event/situation context around the same comment while preserving the FHIR-26678 Period rule.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch. The current build-scope Condition.onset[x] comment already contains the FHIR-26678 wording, so editing source would be redundant.
